<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard Arch Linux package for `fnm-bin`, a precompiled binary release of the `fnm` Node.js version manager. The source URLs correctly point to the official GitHub repository (https://github.com/Schniz/fnm), and each architecture-specific binary is downloaded from the corresponding release page using a predictable and verifiable path. The checksums (sha256sums) are explicitly provided for all architectures, ensuring integrity verification of the downloaded binaries.

The package installation process is straightforward and follows standard packaging practices: it installs the `fnm` binary into `/usr/bin` and generates shell completion scripts for bash, fish, and zsh by invoking the binary with appropriate subcommands. These completions are written to standard system directories, which is a common and safe post-installation step. There are no network requests, file modifications outside the package directory, or execution of external scripts during installation.

All operations occur within the build and packaging environment, targeting only the `$pkgdir` hierarchy. The license, URL, and metadata are consistent with the upstream project. There is no obfuscated code, suspicious commands (e.g., `curl|bash`, `eval`, `base64` decoding), or unexpected behavior. The package adheres to Arch packaging guidelines and poses no evident security risk.
</details>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR (Arch User Repository) to describe the package and its sources. It specifies the package base, version, architecture, license, and source URLs with corresponding checksums. The sources point to official release binaries hosted on GitHub (https://github.com/Schniz/fnm), which is the legitimate upstream project for `fnm`. The checksums (sha256sums) are provided for each architecture and match the expected values for the declared version (1.39.0), ensuring binary integrity.

There are no scripts, commands, or executable logic in this file. It does not perform any network operations, file modifications, or system calls. The use of `::` in the source lines is standard AUR syntax to rename downloaded files and does not indicate obfuscation or redirection. The package provides `fnm`, conflicts with alternative versions (`fnm-git`, `fnm`), and targets supported architectures (x86_64, aarch64, armv7h), all consistent with normal packaging practices.

No evidence of malicious behavior, obfuscation, or supply-chain attack vectors is present. The file strictly serves its role as a package metadata descriptor, referencing verifiable binaries from the official upstream. While the checksums are valid and the sources are legitimate, users should still trust the upstream provider (Schniz/fnm) as the binaries are precompiled and not built from source.
</details>
